weapons.name: Mk-82
weapons.summary: 500 lb low-drag unguided bomb. Simple and cheap; the Mk-83 (1000 lb) and Mk-84 (2000 lb) work the same way. It is also the body used by the GBU-12 laser kit and the GBU-38 JDAM GPS kit.
weapons.bestFor: Soft or lightly-protected targets when air defences let you get close.
weapons.watchOut: CCIP means diving at the target (30–45°), which is risky near air defences. CCRP/AUTO lets you stay level but is less precise.
facts: CCIP (dive, impact point shown) or AUTO/CCRP (level, release cue)
MFUZ NOSE · EFUZ INST (or DLY1 for delay)
FF (low-drag) or RET for the retarded Mk-82SE Snake Eye
Hold RALT+SPACE until all programmed bombs are gone
steps: Master Arm – ARM, Master Mode – A/G
SMS page: select 82B, PROG 1
MODE – CCIP
MFUZ NOSE · EFUZ INST (or DLY1) · DRAG FF or RET
UFC: QTY 2 · MULT 1 · INT 500 ft
Dive 30–45° and line the target up on the DIL (bomb fall line)
Keep the DIL vertical and the CCIP cross on the target
Hold weapon release (RALT+SPACE) until all bombs are off
Pull up before the velocity vector reaches the PULL UP cue

weapons.name: Mk-20 Rockeye
weapons.summary: Unguided 500 lb anti-armour cluster bomb. It bursts at a set height and scatters bomblets over an area, so it forgives aiming errors against groups of vehicles.
weapons.bestFor: Groups of vehicles or armour spread over an area.
weapons.watchOut: Still a CCIP dive delivery. The mechanical fuze must be VT (proximity), or the Height-of-Burst option won't appear.
facts: MFUZ VT (proximity) unlocks the HT option
Toggle with HT; Chuck recommends 1500 ft
steps: Master Arm – ARM, Master Mode – A/G
SMS page: select RE, PROG 1
MODE – CCIP
MFUZ – VT, then HT – 1500 ft
UFC: QTY 2 · MULT 1 · INT 500 ft
Dive 30–45°, target on the DIL
CCIP cross on target: hold RALT+SPACE
Pull up before the PULL UP cue

weapons.name: Rockets
weapons.summary: Unguided rockets fired from pods (LAU-68 shows as 68R). Aim with the CCIP reticle, wait for IN RNG and fire.
weapons.bestFor: Soft targets and light vehicles at short range.
weapons.watchOut: Short range means getting close. Break off as soon as the Breakaway X appears.
facts: 2.75 in general-purpose rockets; Zuni Mk-71 5 in rockets
IN RNG to fire, Breakaway X to stop
steps: Master Arm – ARM, Master Mode – A/G
SMS page: select 68R (boxed)
SGL or SAL, motor type, MODE – CCIP
Reticle on the target, wait for IN RNG
Fire with RALT+SPACE
Break away when the Breakaway X appears

weapons.name: M61A2 Gun
weapons.summary: Six-barrel 20 mm Gatling-type cannon with 578 rounds. Air-to-ground it uses a CCIP reticle. Air-to-air you use the funnel, or the radar's gun auto-acquisition mode for a lead-computing SHOOT cue.
weapons.bestFor: Strafing soft targets, and close-in dogfights when missiles won't work.
weapons.watchOut: A/A without radar: you judge range by fitting the target's wingspan inside the funnel. A/G: break off at the Breakaway X.
facts: GACQ auto-locks targets inside the dashed circle at 5 nm or less
steps: Master Arm – ARM; Weapon Select AFT (LSHIFT+X) for A/A
SMS: rounds type and HI/LO rate
No radar: put the 1000/2000 ft range dot on the target, wingspan filling the funnel
With radar: fly the target into the dashed GACQ circle for an auto-lock
Pipper on target and SHOOT cue: squeeze the trigger (Spacebar)

weapons.name: GBU-38 JDAM
weapons.summary: A Mk-82 with a GPS/INS guidance kit (shows as J-82). It flies itself to a set of coordinates, so it never needs to see the target. Each bomb can be programmed separately to hit several targets in one pass.
weapons.bestFor: Fixed targets with known coordinates, including several targets at once.
weapons.watchOut: Allow about 3 minutes of alignment first. Coordinates need the target elevation too. TOO mode only stores coordinates for one bomb at a time.
facts: About 16 ft (5 m) with good alignment
Type coordinates in by hand; 5 points per station (PP1–PP5)
Uses the current A/G designation (TGP, waypoint, radar)
TMR → IN RNG → IN ZONE (inside the IZLAR)
F10 map in Deg Min Sec.Dec — LALT+Y toggles the format
steps: SMS: select J-82 (ideally on the ground), wait about 3 min for 01 GOOD
Release mode TOO, EFUZ INST, JDAM DSPLY → MAN, QTY and station
MSN page → TOO1
Targeting pod: FLIR STBY, wait about 2 min, then ON
Undesignate ×2 for VVSLV, ×2 again for Snowplow
Slew onto the target, TDC Depress: the coordinates go to the JDAM
Master Arm – ARM, A/G; fly the steering cue to the target diamond
Wait for IN RNG, then IN ZONE
Hold weapon release (RALT+SPACE)

weapons.name: AGM-154 JSOW
weapons.summary: Same GPS/INS guidance as the JDAM, but with wings: it glides much farther, so you can release well outside the defences. The AGM-154A (JSA) is a cluster weapon with an adjustable burst height; the AGM-154C (JSC) has no burst height setting.
weapons.bestFor: Stand-off attacks on area targets without flying over the defences.
weapons.watchOut: After a JSOW leaves, the next one is still aimed at the same designation. Designate the next waypoint before releasing again.
facts: Significantly longer than a JDAM (it glides)
TOO UFC → HT; higher HT = bigger radius (e.g. 100 ft)
Waypoint Designate (WPDSG) on the HSI is the simplest method
HSI DATA: verify waypoint coordinates and elevation; PRECISE adds digits
steps: HSI → DATA: check the target waypoint's coordinates and elevation
SMS: select JSA, wait about 3 min for alignment
TOO, EFUZ INST, JSOW DSPLY → MAN, QTY and stations
MSN → TOO1 → TOO UFC → HT (e.g. 100 ft)
Master Arm – ARM, A/G; HSI on one DDI, JSOW page on the other
HSI: select the target waypoint, press WPDSG
Steer to the diamond until IN RNG
Hold weapon release (RALT+SPACE)
Designate the next waypoint before the next release

weapons.name: GBU-12 Paveway II
weapons.summary: A laser-guided Mk-82. It follows reflected laser energy with a specific code, so the bomb, the targeting pod and the SMS all have to agree on the same code.
weapons.bestFor: Precise hits on fixed or slow targets you can see with the targeting pod.
weapons.watchOut: The laser must stay on the target until impact. The bomb's code is set by the ground crew (default 1688). After the target dies the laser goes back to SAFE and must be re-armed.
facts: Bomb code = TGP LTDC code = SMS CODE
CCIP or AUTO (the guide uses AUTO)
MFUZ OFF · EFUZ INST or DLY1
TRIG unboxed: the laser fires automatically before impact
steps: Ground crew: confirm the GBU-12 laser code (default 1688)
Master Arm – ARM, A/G; SMS → 82LG, PROG 1, MODE AUTO
MFUZ OFF · EFUZ INST (or DLY1)
Targeting pod on; designate the target
TGP UFC → LTDC: set the same code (1688)
SMS → CODE: set the bomb's code (1688)
Fly level along the ASL, release at the cue (hold RALT+SPACE)
Keep the laser on target until impact (auto-lase with TRIG off)

weapons.name: AGM-65F/G Maverick (IR)
weapons.summary: Missile with an imaging infrared seeker, usable at night and in bad weather. Lock a contrasting target with the seeker, fire, and it guides itself.
weapons.bestFor: Vehicles and armour, including moving ones; works at night.
weapons.watchOut: The seeker must be cooled for about 3 minutes, and cooling only starts once you're airborne. At the gimbal limits the seeker cages itself.
facts: About 3 min; starts when MAVF is selected in the air
Slave it to the targeting pod or the GMT radar track
The seeker cages itself at its limits
steps: Airborne: SMS → select MAVF, wait about 3 min for cooling
Show the MAVF feed, Sensor Control toward it
Fuze INST / DLY1 / DLY2
Uncage (Cage/Uncage button)
Hold TDC Depress, slew onto the target, release to lock
Locked (MAVF no longer crossed out): fire with RALT+SPACE

weapons.name: AGM-65E Maverick (Laser)
weapons.summary: Laser-homing Maverick with a heavier penetrating blast-fragmentation warhead, optimised for fortified installations. Unlike the GBU-12, its laser code can be set from the cockpit.
weapons.bestFor: Hardened or fortified targets, and targets lased by a JTAC or wingman.
weapons.watchOut: Its code must match the laser that is guiding it, and the laser must stay on until impact.
facts: Set in the cockpit: MAV DSPLY → UFC → CODE (example 1456)
TTMR counts down to in range, then IN RNG
Uncage to search; MAV LKD = locked on a laser
steps: Airborne, Master Arm – ARM, A/G; SMS → MAV (wait about 30 s)
MAV DSPLY → UFC → CODE (e.g. 1456)
Targeting pod on; designate the target
TGP UFC → LTDC: the same code (1456); TRIG unboxed for auto-lase
Sensor Control to the MAV page, uncage
At IN RNG, hold RALT+SPACE; the laser fires automatically

weapons.name: AGM-88C HARM
weapons.summary: Homes on the radio emissions of radars, which makes it the main weapon for SEAD (suppression of enemy air defences). Pick an emitter on the HARM display or RWR and fire; no range information is given.
weapons.watchOut: Altitude extends the range a lot, but it also makes you easier to see. Keep countermeasures ready and break away after firing.
facts: Up to 80 nm; much better from high altitude (30,000 ft+)
Select an emitter (RAID/FLIR FOV, I), uncage to hand off
Self-protect: quick shots, 360° but costs energy
Unbox HRM OVRD: a HARM is readied automatically against a critical threat
Pre-briefed: designate the expected location + threat code (e.g. 117 = SA-8)
The HARM gives no range to target in TOO/SP
steps: Master Arm – ARM, A/G; EW page right DDI, SMS left
SMS → HARM, mode TOO
Sensor Control to the HARM page
Pick the emitter with RAID/FLIR FOV (I)
Turn to centre it, uncage → H-OFF (handoff)
Fire (RALT+SPACE), then break away

weapons.name: AGM-84D Harpoon
weapons.summary: All-weather, over-the-horizon anti-ship missile. Fly it out on a bearing (BOL), or at a designated point (R/BL), and it searches for a ship when it gets there.
weapons.watchOut: Launch above 2500 ft and level; negative G can bring the missile into the aircraft. A brief radar altimeter warning after launch is normal.
facts: Bearing-only: search distance (0–105 nm), self-destruct distance, bearing
Range & bearing to a designated point (WPDSG, TGP or SEA radar)
SKIM (sea-skimming) or POP (pop-up, hits from above)
Above 2500 ft, level, no negative G
steps: Master Arm – ARM, A/G; SMS → HPD (about 25 s alignment)
UFC: SRCH (search distance), destruct distance, bearing
FLT LOW/MED/HIGH, TERM SKIM or POP
Optional: HPTP turnpoint or FXP fixpoint
Check IN ZONE, above 2500 ft, level
Hold RALT+SPACE to launch

weapons.name: AGM-84E SLAM
weapons.summary: Subsonic, over-the-horizon cruise missile built from the Harpoon, adding GPS, a Walleye-style TV seeker and a datalink. It flies out on its own; near the target you watch its video and steer it in.
weapons.bestFor: High-value fixed targets deep in defended areas; ships in TOO mode.
weapons.watchOut: Needs the AWW-13 datalink pod. Pick a sensible DIST (when the seeker activates), and don't fly in the same direction as the missile.
facts: Distance from target when the seeker goes active (e.g. 15 nm)
Hold TDC Depress and slew the crosshair onto the target
steps: Master Arm – ARM, A/G; SMS → SLAM, DL13 on (about 3 min alignment)
WEP: pair the datalink pod with the SLAM station
FLT MED, EFUZ INST, SLAM DSPLY → REL TYPE MAN
UFC → DIST 15 nm
MODE TOO → MSN → TOO1; designate the target (e.g. WPDSG)
Fly to IN RNG, hold RALT+SPACE
When TTS reaches 0 the video goes live; wait for the terminal dive
Hold TDC Depress, slew the crosshair onto the target, release

weapons.name: AGM-84H SLAM-ER
weapons.summary: The longer-range SLAM: about 150 nm, and it can fly through intermediate steerpoints. Fire-and-forget at coordinates, or steer its infrared seeker yourself, which also allows moving targets.
weapons.bestFor: Very long stand-off strikes, routed around defences.
weapons.watchOut: Long flight times — the guide suggests the autopilot while you wait. Slewing the X freezes the video until you release TDC Depress.
facts: Lets you attack a moving target
Slew the X with TDC Depress held (video freezes while slewing)
steps: SMS → SLMR, DL13 on (about 3 min alignment); WEP pairing
FLT, EFUZ INST, SLMR DSPLY → MAN, DIST 15 nm
TOO1 ← WPDSG on the target waypoint
STP: assign intermediate steerpoints (waypoints)
Fly to IN RNG, launch; consider autopilot
TTS = 0: the seeker is live; slew the X onto the target in the terminal dive

weapons.name: AGM-62 Walleye II
weapons.full: AGM-62 Walleye II ER/DL TV-guided glide bomb
needs: AWW-13 datalink pod (only to steer it)
weapons.summary: 2000 lb TV-guided glide bomb. Without a pod it's fire-and-forget like an IR Maverick; with the AWW-13 datalink pod you can steer it all the way by its video.
weapons.bestFor: Large fixed targets from a few miles out, in daylight.
weapons.watchOut: Only on stations 2 and 8. When steering it, stay high and fast (20,000 ft+) and don't over-control — it's heavy and loses energy fast.
facts: Usable from 20 nm; good lock usually inside 10 miles
No lock needed to launch (but recommended)
Launch at 20,000 ft+ with good speed when remote-steering
steps: Master Arm – ARM, A/G; SMS → WEDL, then WEDL again for the feed
Fuze INST or DLY; Sensor Control to the feed
Uncage, hold TDC Depress and slew onto the target, release to lock
Locked (WE no longer crossed out): hold RALT+SPACE

weapons.name: ADM-141A TALD
weapons.summary: A gliding decoy that looks like an aircraft to enemy radars. SAM sites fire at it and reveal themselves — the perfect moment for your HARMs.
weapons.bestFor: Saturating air defences and making SAMs turn on, as part of a SEAD package.
weapons.watchOut: It does no damage on its own; pair it with HARMs.
facts: 2, 3, 7 and 8 on BRU-42 racks, up to 3 per rack
SAMs fire at the TALDs, revealing their positions for HARMs
steps: Master Arm – ARM, A/G
SMS → 82P, STEP between stations
Press RALT+SPACE to launch; it glides as far as it can
Hunt the SAMs that reveal themselves with HARMs

weapons.name: AIM-9M Sidewinder
weapons.summary: Heat-seeking dogfight missile. Uncage it, put the target in the seeker circle and listen: a low growl means searching, a high-pitched tone means locked.
weapons.watchOut: Cool the seeker first (IR COOL – NORM). With a radar lock, fire slightly inside RNE (no-escape range) for the best chance.
facts: IR COOL – NORM; coolant lasts about 3 hours
Low growl = searching · high pitch = locked
ACM modes BST / VACQ / WACQ auto-lock within 5 nm
steps: IR COOL – NORM
Master Arm – ARM; Weapon Select DOWN (LSHIFT+S)
Uncage with C; listen for the growl
Put the target in the seeker circle until the high-pitched tone
Squeeze the trigger (Spacebar)

weapons.name: AIM-9X Sidewinder
weapons.summary: An upgraded Sidewinder with thrust vectoring: with the JHMCS helmet you can look at a target up to 80° off the nose and shoot it.
weapons.bestFor: Dogfights where the target is way off your nose.
weapons.watchOut: Learn the tones: static = searching, steady tone = sees a target, higher pitch = uncaged.
facts: Up to 80° with thrust vector control
Put the DAC (Dynamic Aiming Cue) and seeker circle on the target
Static: searching · steady: sees a target · steady high: uncaged
steps: IR COOL – NORM; HMD – BRT
Master Arm – ARM; Weapon Select DOWN (LSHIFT+S)
Look at the target: DAC and seeker circle on it
Hold Cage/Uncage (C); the circle shrinks and the tone goes high
Squeeze the trigger (Spacebar)

weapons.name: AIM-7M Sparrow
weapons.summary: Semi-active radar-guided missile: it homes on your radar's reflection from the target, so you must keep the target locked until impact.
weapons.bestFor: Beyond-visual-range shots when you can keep the lock.
weapons.watchOut: Not fire-and-forget: if your lock breaks, the missile is lost. LOFT mode trades a higher path for more energy at the end.
facts: NORM, LOFT (higher, thinner air, more energy), HELO
RWS: TDC over the contact, TDC Depress
Steering dot in the ASE circle, SHOOT cue, trigger
SMS shows RMIN / RMAX / RNE, TOF, closure
steps: Radar – OPR; RDR ATTK on the right DDI, SMS on the left
Master Arm – ARM; Weapon Select FWD (LSHIFT+W)
SMS: target size, MODE NORM
TDC over the contact, TDC Depress to lock (STT)
Steering dot in the ASE circle; SHOOT cue → trigger
Keep the lock until impact

weapons.name: AIM-120B AMRAAM
weapons.summary: Active radar homing missile: your radar guides it at first, then its own radar takes over ("Pitbull") and it's truly fire-and-forget.
weapons.bestFor: Beyond-visual-range fights, including shots on several targets.
weapons.watchOut: Without a lock it launches "Mad Dog" and attacks the first thing its seeker finds within 10 miles — including friendlies.
facts: The missile's own radar goes active: fire-and-forget (brevity: Fox Three on launch)
Time until the missile goes active
No lock: seeker takes the first target in the dashed circle out to 10 miles
RMIN · RNE · RMAX on the HUD
steps: Radar – OPR; RDR ATTK on the right DDI, SMS on the left
Master Arm – ARM; Weapon Select RIGHT (LSHIFT+D)
SMS: expected target size (RCS)
TDC over the contact, TDC Depress to lock
Steering dot in the ASE circle; SHOOT cue → hold the trigger
